Renumber a pedigree in topological order

Source: R/renum_pedigree.R
renum_pedigree.Rd

Assigns consecutive integer IDs (1..N) to animals in a pedigree, ensuring that parents always receive a lower ID than their offspring. This is a prerequisite for building the numerator relationship matrix inverse (A-inverse) via build_Ainv().

renum_pedigree(
  pedigree,
  unknown_parent = c("0", "00000000000000"),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

pedigree

A data frame or data.table with exactly three columns in order: animal ID, sire ID, dam ID. Column names are ignored; only position matters. IDs can be character or numeric.

unknown_parent

Character vector of codes used to denote unknown parents. Defaults to c("0", "00000000000000"). All codes are recoded to "0" internally.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE (default), prints iteration progress to stderr.

Value

A data frame with columns:

new_id

Integer. New consecutive ID for the animal (1..N).

new_sire

Integer. New ID of the sire (0 = unknown).

new_dam

Integer. New ID of the dam (0 = unknown).

animal

Character. Original animal ID.

sire

Character. Original sire ID.

dam

Character. Original dam ID.

Rows are sorted by new_id. Animals that could not be renumbered (due to missing parents or cycles) are excluded with a warning.

Details

The algorithm performs iterative topological sorting: in each iteration it includes all animals whose parents have already been assigned an ID. This handles arbitrary pedigree depths without recursion.

Examples

ped <- data.frame(
  animal = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  sire   = c("0", "0", "A", "A"),
  dam    = c("0", "0", "B", "B")
)
renum_pedigree(ped)
#>   Iteration    1:      2 animals included (total:        2)
#>   Iteration    2:      2 animals included (total:        4)
#>   new_id new_sire new_dam animal sire dam
#> A      1        0       0      A    0   0
#> B      2        0       0      B    0   0
#> C      3        1       2      C    A   B
#> D      4        1       2      D    A   B
